clue.text: Before church, good brother pipes music

indicators.note: the good brother comes before the church, so those letters lead and the church abbreviation closes

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is the crossword abbreviation for good
bro is a casual short form of brother

explanation.surface: A pious monk plays the bagpipes outside a church before the service starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A pibroch is a set of classical variations played on the Scottish Highland bagpipe.

clue.text: In school, brave but humourless

indicators.note: the brave goes in the school, held between its letters

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
to face something is to brave it

explanation.surface: A pupil at school who is courageous but has no sense of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is a group of whales, not a place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone po-faced is solemn and disapproving, lacking any lightness.

clue.text: In India, there's prohibition aplenty

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase locating a city within India

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
galore means in abundance, aplenty

explanation.surface: In India there is plenty of banning going on.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangalore (now Bengaluru) is a large city in southern India.

clue.text: Nothing pleasant is held back

parts.note: O, the zero shape, stands for nothing
nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: No pleasant feeling is being restrained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' is a link; 'held back' is the definition, meaning postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans put on ice are suspended or deferred until later.

clue.text: Rugby player as a comic figure

explanation.surface: A rugby player acting the clown.
explanation.walkthrough: Harlequins is a London rugby union club.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Harlequins club is one; the masked, motley-clad clown of pantomime and commedia dell'arte is the other.

clue.text: In rag, found a line of gossip

indicators.note: the line is placed in the rag, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a tatter is a torn rag of cloth

explanation.surface: Someone finds a line of scandal printed in a trashy newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rag' suggests a tabloid paper, but here it is a scrap of cloth; 'found a' is only linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattler is a person who chatters and spreads rumours, a talebearer.

clue.text: Clemens non Papa?

parts.note: a Clemens who was never Pope: the writer Samuel Clemens, by his pen name, rather than a Pope Clement

explanation.surface: The name of the Flemish composer Clemens non Papa, so called to distinguish him from the Pope.
explanation.walkthrough: Clemens non Papa was a real 16th-century composer; here the Clemens who was not the Pope is Samuel Clemens, the American author.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was the pen name of Samuel Langhorne Clemens.

clue.text: Unnecessary weight above lid on food container

parts.note: a top is a lid
a hamper is a basket for food

explanation.surface: Too much heavy stuff sitting on the lid of a picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is a link placing one piece before the other in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-hamper is the gear and rigging aloft on a ship, seen as burdensome weight overhead.

clue.text: Being prone to perjury

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to commit perjury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prone to' looks like 'inclined to'; split it: 'Being prone' is lying flat, and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying means stretched out flat, and also telling untruths, as perjury under oath is.

clue.text: Old royal holding container of eye-liner

indicators.note: the old royal holds the container, which sits inside it

parts.note: the real was an old Spanish coin, its name meaning royal
a tin is a container

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch holding a pot of eye make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye-liner' looks like make-up, but means the eye's lining; retinal is the adjective from it, used loosely here. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina lines the back of the eyeball, so retinal relates to that lining layer.

clue.text: Trouble if gun rusts

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so the letters of if gun are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A gun left to rust will give its owner trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' and 'rusts' both look like verbs about a gun; 'rusts' is the plural noun, plant diseases.
explanation.definitionFit: Rusts are parasitic plant diseases caused by fungal organisms, so they are examples of the class.

clue.text: Gather mark and enter for following term

parts.note: to reap is to gather in a harvest
a point is a mark or dot

explanation.surface: Instructions to gather marks and register for the next school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Term' suggests a school term, but the definition means installing someone in office for a further period.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappoint someone is to name them to their post again for another stint of office.

clue.text: African creature unlikely to stay still in shade

definitions.text: African creature unlikely to stay still in shade

parts.words: African creature unlikely to stay still in shade
parts.note: describes a lizard that keeps altering its colour, never holding one hue or tint for long

explanation.surface: An animal that refuses to rest quietly in the shadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade' reads as shelter from the sun but means a colour; the lizard changes its tint rather than its position.
explanation.definitionFit: This lizard, common in Africa, is famous for changing its skin colour to match its surroundings.

clue.text: Old ship bearing a noble sort of air

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth
N, north, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: An ancient ship with an aristocratic air about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noble' points to aristocrats, but here it is the chemist's noble (inert) gas, one of the components of air.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is an inert noble gas making up nearly one per cent of the atmosphere.

clue.text: Refuse to sleep rough around the end of December

indicators.note: the dossing goes around the last letter, enclosing it inside

parts.note: to doss is to sleep rough, in makeshift quarters

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here of December

explanation.surface: Someone declines to sleep on the streets as December closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like the verb to decline; it is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is worthless waste matter, rubbish or scum.

clue.text: Fictional servant appears correctly in uniform with regiment

indicators.note: the correctly word goes in the uniform word, enclosed by it

parts.note: uniform as an adjective means the same throughout
well means correctly, properly
R is an abbreviation for regiment

explanation.surface: A servant turns up properly dressed in the uniform of a regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like a noun, clothes; it is the adjective SAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's cockney manservant in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers.

clue.text: Unusual cut in play is restored

indicators.note: the letters of cut in play are put back together in a different order

explanation.surface: A scene cut from a play is unusually put back in.
explanation.definitionFit: Untypical is an equivalent of atypical, meaning out of the ordinary or rare.

clue.text: To excel can start to seem wildly in fashion

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit in the fashion word, enclosed by it

parts.note: a trend is a fashion

indicators.note: wildly means the word can and one letter are thrown about into a new order
the start to a word is its first letter, here of seem

explanation.surface: To be outstanding, a can may appear wildly fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' belongs to the definition, not the selection; 'wildly' scrambles the can with the opening letter of seem, and 'in' sets that jumble inside the word for fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To transcend is to surpass or go beyond, as to outdo others.

clue.text: The spirit of old Geneva?

parts.note: the spirit here is a doctrine or creed, the reformed theology preached in that Swiss city in the sixteenth century

explanation.surface: A question about the drink or soul of an old Swiss city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' tempts toward gin (named from genever), but the question mark points to the religious outlook of John Calvin's Geneva.
explanation.definitionFit: The Protestant theology of John Calvin was centred on his reform of the church in Geneva.

clue.text: Fresh cut to the ear — one gets a nasty infection

indicators.note: the words fresh cut are heard rather than seen, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: freshly cut grass is new-mown
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A freshly cut finger, and someone picks up a horrible infection.
explanation.walkthrough: NEW-MOWN said aloud gives the start of the answer, then I (one) and A follow; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pneumonia is a serious inflammation of the lungs caused by bacteria or viruses.

clue.text: Take trouble over baby's first vegetable

parts.note: pother means fuss or trouble

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word baby's

explanation.surface: Go to trouble over a baby's first solid food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' and 'over' are links; in a down clue the baby's letter follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot-herb is a leafy plant grown for cooking, such as greens for the pot.

clue.text: Roman priest held object of veneration

indicators.note: the priest is held inside the Roman letters, enclosed by them

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic
Eli is the priest of the Temple in the Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A Roman Catholic priest holds up a sacred object.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is a favourite crossword priest, the one who raised Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a saint's remains or belongings kept and revered as holy.

clue.text: Steely work involving cruelty

indicators.note: involving in its old sense of twisting or entangling, so the letters of cruelty are tangled into another order

explanation.surface: A hard-hearted act of cruelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steely' suggests a cold manner; it means made of steel, as knives and forks are.
explanation.definitionFit: Knives, forks and spoons are typically steel goods, the work of the Sheffield trade.

clue.text: Lie around black board

indicators.note: the lie goes around the black, holding it inside

parts.note: a tale is a lie or fib
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Lying around a blackboard in a classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black board' tempts as one word; 'board' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Board can mean a table, especially one where meals are served.

clue.text: Simple, or extract of herb, as I call it

indicators.note: an extract is a portion taken out, so a run of letters is drawn from the words that follow

explanation.surface: Simple, or a herbal extract, as I would put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extract of herb' looks like a herbal remedy; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means elementary or plain, without frills.

clue.text: Stomach is churning — he enjoys it?

indicators.note: a churning stomach is turned over, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A man's stomach churns, yet he seems to like the feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'it' is pain or suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone of this type takes pleasure in pain or humiliation.

clue.text: Note rises and falls

indicators.note: reading upward and downward in the grid gives the same letters, so the word goes up and comes back down unchanged

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A musical note climbs and then drops.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'rises' is read bottom to top; the word is the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a half note in music, lasting two crotchets.

clue.text: Driving instructor?

parts.note: read as someone who instructs, a trainer, who is also a driver of a horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: A question about someone who gives driving lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns against a simple driving teacher: it is a sports trainer, and also the carriage someone drives.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a trainer or tutor, and also a large vehicle driven by a coachman.

clue.text: Wood work — schoolboy and girl take a hand

parts.note: East is Tom Brown's schoolfellow in Tom Brown's Schooldays
Lynn is a girl's name
E, East, is one of the four hands at bridge

explanation.surface: In woodwork class, a boy and girl each lend a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood work' suggests carpentry, but Wood is the novelist Mrs Henry Wood; at bridge the players are named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: East Lynne is the best-known novel by the Victorian author Ellen Wood (Mrs Henry Wood).

clue.text: A dishonest approach, but it had style

explanation.surface: A shady chat-up, though it was delivered with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: To spin someone a line is to deceive them; the second reading is a dress cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A line is a smooth deceptive patter; an A-line is a fashion cut flaring from a narrow top, like a letter.

clue.text: Cloth for binding two animals

parts.note: a buck is a male deer or rabbit
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Fabric used to tie up a pair of beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Binding' suggests tying up animals; it means bookbinding.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a stiff coarse cotton or linen used for covering books.

clue.text: Back in twenty-four hours from Africa

definitions.note: the definition names a place from Africa, an old West African kingdom

indicators.note: the home is placed in the day, enclosed by it

parts.note: a day lasts twenty-four hours
to be back is to be home again

explanation.surface: A traveller promises to be back from Africa within a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like part of 'back in twenty-four hours', but it gives HOME on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahomey is the former name of Benin, a West African country.
